QuantumBridge — Live Circuit Reliability Predictor

Pick a real IBM chip layout and any two qubits, and get a Bell-pair circuit's predicted execution success from two models: v4.1, a hand-derived closed-form physics model, and GNN, a graph neural network. Kyiv and Sherbrooke predictions come from a model trained on those two chips with a calibrated MC-Dropout uncertainty band (shown as ±). Brisbane predictions come from a separate model trained on all three chips pooled together (Entry 065) -- it performs comparably well but does not yet have a validated uncertainty estimate, and is labeled as such. Where available, the actual simulated hardware result is shown alongside for comparison.
24,003 qubit pairs covered (3 chips) 4,886 circuits in combined training data 127 qubits per chip (Kyiv, Sherbrooke & Brisbane) 2,737 GNN parameters

What this is, honestly: every prediction shown is a real output from the actual trained model and the actual closed-form formula — nothing here is faked or approximated for the demo. But the underlying noise data comes from Qiskit's "fake backend" snapshots of real IBM device calibration, run through Aer's noise simulator — not live queued jobs on physical hardware. Ground truth is only available for the subset of pairs that were actually simulated (about 1,600 of the 16,002 shown here); the rest show model predictions only, clearly marked. The ± range next to the GNN prediction is a genuine uncertainty estimate (MC-Dropout, 20 stochastic forward passes per pair) -- it widens on circuit types and chip regions the model is less confident about, not a cosmetic error bar. This is an early-stage academic project (undergraduate research), not a production tool. Built with Qiskit, JAX/Optax, and a from-scratch graph neural network.
